intervals.label: CESR data taking (north area)
intervals.locator: Berkelman, chapter 10 (The CLEO-2 Years); "since the turn-on of CESR in 1979" (chapter 5)
intervals.note: Start: CUSB had run "since the turn-on of CESR in 1979"; the month is taken from the first colliding-beam luminosity on 14 August 1979 (chapter 3); end derived as 1979 + eleven years (the PAC terminated CUSB after one more Υ(4S) run in the early CLEO-2 era). CUSB-II (BGO upgrade) was chosen by the PAC in January 1984.
intervals.quote: CUSB under the leadership of the Franzinis had run in the north interaction region for eleven years

intervals.label: CUSB terminated
intervals.note: Year derived (see the active interval); the detector was dismantled afterwards.
intervals.quote: Upon the advice of the PAC I decided to terminate the CUSB experiment after one more run on the Υ(4S).

placements.note: Campus-grade placement: no fetched source locates the CLEO or CUSB experimental areas; the marker is the Wilson Laboratory building point. CUSB sat at the north interaction point, in trailers on Upper Alumni Field.
placements.quote: The users of CESR in the 1980’s were CLEO at the south interaction point, CUSB in the north, CHESS

summary.plain: The CUSB detector: a compact non-magnetic ball of sodium iodide and lead glass crystals that measured the energies of photons from Upsilon decays at the north interaction point of CESR.
summary.technical: CUSB: non-magnetic NaI and lead-glass shower detector (CUSB-II: BGO scintillation counters replacing the tracking chambers).

technology.quote: running their nonmagnetic NaI and lead-glass detector there since the turn-on of CESR in 1979
technology.value: Non-magnetic NaI and lead-glass shower detector
